hunt.justification: Autonomous AI agents compress attack cycles from days to hours. Detecting the unique reasoning and velocity markers of these agents is essential for intercepting an intrusion before it completes exfiltration.

meta.name: Agentic AI Autonomous Behavioral Patterns

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the speed and reasoning of the operator behind the shell, not the shell's presence itself.

meta.analysis: AI agents generate unique commands on the fly; static rules for web shells fail to capture the autonomous reasoning loop and inhuman speed that this hunt identifies through multi-surface behavioral analysis.

stages.name: Initial access via web shell
observables: web shell installation via vulnerable web application

stages.name: Autonomous AI agent execution
observables: reasoning comments in scripts (e.g. # Step 1: Enumerating users)

stages.name: Iterative privilege escalation
observables: on-target compilation of kernel exploits using gcc
sequential attempts of 5+ different privesc techniques

scenario.summary: Multiple global campaigns involve human operators gaining initial access via web shells on vulnerable web applications before handing control to autonomous AI agents. These agents then execute reconnaissance, iterative privilege escalation (including kernel exploit compilation), and lateral movement at machine speed, characterized by distinct behavioral markers like section headers and reasoning comments in scripts.

meta.rationale: Focus the hunt on internet-facing Linux and Windows servers where web shells are the primary entry point for agentic operators.
meta.hypothesis: An autonomous AI agent is conducting an intrusion, evidenced by inhuman command velocity, structured section headers in shell output, and chain-of-thought reasoning comments within script telemetry.

c2_ips.description: C2 and relay IPs associated with GSocket and SSH tunneling in agentic campaigns.

scope_hosts.description: Hostnames to scope; leave empty to hunt the whole estate.

references.name: Unit 42 — Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks

blind_spots.risk: Large script blocks containing AI reasoning may be truncated, removing the primary behavioral fingerprint of the agent.
blind_spots.question: Are the reasoning comments captured in full by the EDR?
blind_spots.remediation: Audit script block logging limits and ensure interpreters are fully monitored.

blind_spots.risk: If telemetry timestamps are rounded to the nearest second, velocity-based detection loses precision.
blind_spots.question: Can we reliably distinguish the 1.4s AI gap from 20s human gap?

hunt.name: Agentic AI Autonomous Behavioral Patterns
hunt.description: The phased flow starts by scoping to vulnerable hosts likely to be targeted for kernel exploitation, then pivots to detect the unique behavioral markers of AI-driven execution before hunting for follow-on cloud reconnaissance and protocol tunneling. The adversary gains initial access via web shells and hands off control to an autonomous AI agent that operates at machine speed. The hunt first identifies vulnerable hosts prone to iterative privilege escalation attempts. It then searches for the unmistakable behavioral markers of agentic AI: an inhuman inter-command gap and reasoning comments embedded in shell scripts. The analyst reviews these automated triggers before pivoting to cloud-level discovery and network tunneling to confirm an active intrusion.

config.rationale: An autonomous AI agent is conducting an intrusion, evidenced by inhuman command velocity, structured section headers in shell output, and chain-of-thought reasoning comments within script telemetry.

nodes.label: Scope to hosts vulnerable to kernel exploits

config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, title FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE (cve_uid = 'CVE-2024-1086' OR cve_uid = 'CVE-2026-31431') AND status != 'suppressed'
config.description: Identify Linux hosts carrying vulnerabilities that AI agents target for rapid, iterative privilege escalation.
config.expected_signal: A list of vulnerable device IDs. These are the high-priority targets where an agent may attempt compilation of custom exploits.

primitive_config.label: Scope to hosts vulnerable to kernel exploits
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, title FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE (cve_uid = 'CVE-2024-1086' OR cve_uid = 'CVE-2026-31431') AND status != 'suppressed'
primitive_config.expected: A list of vulnerable device IDs. These are the high-priority targets where an agent may attempt compilation of custom exploits.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, parent_process_name, COUNT(*) AS total_commands, COUNT(DISTINCT process_name) AS unique_commands, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name, parent_process_name HAVING unique_commands > 100 ORDER BY total_commands DESC
config.description: Identify hosts where a single parent launches hundreds of unique children in a tight window, indicating automated agent control.
config.expected_signal: Hosts with hundreds of unique commands from a single parent. A median gap analysis by an analyst can confirm the 1.4s velocity mentioned in the report.

primitive_config.label: Inhuman command execution velocity
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, parent_process_name, COUNT(*) AS total_commands, COUNT(DISTINCT process_name) AS unique_commands, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name, parent_process_name HAVING unique_commands > 100 ORDER BY total_commands DESC
primitive_config.expected: Hosts with hundreds of unique commands from a single parent. A median gap analysis by an analyst can confirm the 1.4s velocity mentioned in the report.

nodes.label: Reasoning comments and section headers in scripts

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_type, script_name, script_content, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%===[%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%thought:%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%reasoning:%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%step 1:%' OR instr(',' || '{{ai_script_markers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(script_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect scripts containing conversational comments or machine-readable headers used by AI agents to navigate and parse their own results.
config.expected_signal: Script contents showing 'chain-of-thought' reasoning or filenames from the ai_script_markers list. These markers are high-fidelity indicators of an autonomous operator.

primitive_config.label: Reasoning comments and section headers in scripts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_type, script_name, script_content, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%===[%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%thought:%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%reasoning:%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%step 1:%' OR instr(',' || '{{ai_script_markers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(script_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Script contents showing 'chain-of-thought' reasoning or filenames from the ai_script_markers list. These markers are high-fidelity indicators of an autonomous operator.

config.objective: Examine the volume of unique commands and the presence of structured reasoning or headers. Decide if this pattern represents an autonomous agent rather than a human administrator or a static script.
config.description: Weigh the velocity and the AI markers together to determine if an autonomous agent is active on any host.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict on whether the observed behavior is agentic AI.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious or suspicious for hosts showing the 'agentic' footprint.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, api_service_name, api_operation, COUNT(*) AS call_count FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE (api_operation LIKE 'List%' OR api_operation LIKE 'Describe%' OR api_operation LIKE 'Get%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, api_service_name, api_operation HAVING call_count > 50 ORDER BY call_count DESC
config.description: Identify high-volume cloud API calls indicating the strategic discovery phase directed by the AI agent.
config.expected_signal: High-volume discovery calls from a single IP or user account. These represent the automated mapping of the target environment.
